newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Big European ICI buy seen unlikely.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Big European ICI buy seen unlikely.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc will probably make more small asset buys like one unveiled on Friday, but a major European acquisition is unlikely, analysts said.
ICI said it bought Rutz und Huber AG's Swiss refinish and commercial transport paints business in a deal valued at less than one percent of the chemicals giant's net assets.
Rutz and Huber had annual turnover of more than 3.0 million pounds ($5.11 million), the firm said.
News of the deal followed a newspaper report -- largely dismissed by chemicals analysts -- which said ICI had lined up a major European acquisition.
Citing unnamed sources, the Daily Mail reported that ICI was planning to help fund a large European acquisition with a possible rights issue of about 1.0 billion pounds.
But analysts dismissed the report, noting that it was no secret ICI wanted to expand its paints business, which made up about 11 percent of its trading profits in 1995.
"I think that someone's probably adding one and one together and getting three or four," said SocGen analyst Paul Diggle.
An ICI spokesman declined to comment on the report, while the company's shares rebounded 9.5 pence to 769.5 by 1130 GMT after falling on Thursday.

Analysts said a rights issue of the size stated in the report would indicate a deal worth a total of more than 2.0 billion pounds and possibly as much as 3.0 to 4.0 billion pounds -- severely limiting any list of possible takeover targets.
"Offhand, I can't think of an entire European company that would meet the criteria that ICI is attempting to set for itself," Diggle said.
Chief executive Charles Miller Smith told an ICI in-house publication recently that businesses representing 1.0-1.5 billion pounds of paint sales were on the market.
"ICI should have some significant proportion of what is on offer in the next 10 years," he said in the interview.
He added that the company's coatings and materials divisions would lead the planned shift in ICI's portfolio away from the heavier end of the chemicals spectrum.
However, analysts doubted the company would seek to accomplish that through a big European acquisition.
"But I certainly wouldn't rule out them getting together with one of the other majors in Europe and maybe doing some asset swaps or buying some product lines," Diggle said.
Another analyst agreed, adding that he expected the modestly-geared firm to use debt to fund any acquisitions.

"They've got plenty of firepower in their balance sheet. So they'll use their balance sheet for acquisitions of up to a billion pounds, possibly two billion, without going to shareholders," the analyst said, declining to be named.
Analysts said ICI might seek to expand its speciality businesses by buying some assets from major German companies looking to make divestments, such as Bayer AG, Hoechst AG, and possibly BASF AG.
"A big jump would be difficult, although I can see them making smaller acquisitions," Diggle said.
